data.title: mSin1 is necessary for Akt/PKB phosphorylation, and its isoforms define three distinct mTORC2s
data.authors: Frias MA; Thoreen CC; Jaffe JD; Schroder W; Sculley T; Carr SA; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mSin1 is required for mTORC2 assembly and Akt Ser473 phosphorylation; isoforms define distinct complexes.
data.abstract_excerpt: The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) is a serine/threonine kinase that participates in at least two distinct multiprotein complexes, mTORC1 and mTORC2 . These complexes play important roles in the regulation of cell growth, proliferation, survival, and metabolism. mTORC2 is a hydrophobic motif kinase for the cell-survival protein Akt/PKB and, here, we identify mSin1 as a component of mTORC2 but not mTORC1. mSin1 is necessary for the assembly of mTORC2 and for its capacity to phosphorylate Akt/PKB.
